contentBlocks.body: A monetary report should keep its unit clear. This database stores integer cents, so each line's value is price_cents times stock and the category total is a SUM. GROUP BY changes the result grain from one product to one category. A category with products but no stock still has value zero; an empty database has no category groups.

contentBlocks.code:
CREATE TABLE products(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, sku TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(price_cents >= 0), stock INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(stock >= 0), reorder_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'BOOK','office',250,5,5),(2,'MUG','home',900,0,2),(3,'PEN','office',150,20,5);

-- Inspect the fixture first, then write your query.
SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id;

The required result is [{"category":"home","value_cents":0},{"category":"office","value_cents":4250}]. Before running code, explain which input values contribute to the result and which are excluded. Then change one boundary value and predict whether the result changes.

**Your task.** Return category and value_cents for every category, ordered by category.
SUM(price_cents) ignores the quantity on hand.

**Check your understanding.** Which boundary case would fail if the main comparison, join, or ordering were changed? Write the reason in your own words before opening the solution. Run the additional cases as well as the visible example: the changed business data case checks a different boundary.
